name: Integration puzzle that snaps together
description: Represent connected products or integrations as a satisfying assembly. Builds an editable 10-second vertical ad from your images, logo and copy. AI can suggest options from a website to fill the fields with its copy and images. No generated video.
tagline: Assembly is a useful metaphor for supported integrations or components.

operations.name: Suggest options from a website
operations.agentTask: Read the website in `sourceUrl` and write three different ways to fill the ad "Integration puzzle that snaps together". Objective: Represent connected products or integrations as a satisfying assembly. Visual rule: Separate elements become one coherent object; the assembly is the proof metaphor, not the actual proof of integration. Beats, in order: - 0–1.5 s: Separated tiles or a partly assembled object are already visible. Shows Brand color, Tile 1, Tile 2, Tile 3, Tile 4, Problem. - 1.5–4 s: Tiles move toward their assigned cells. Shows Brand color, Tile 1, Tile 2, Tile 3, Tile 4, Connection line. - 4–6.5 s: The completed object rotates slightly or pulses once. Shows Brand color, Tile 1, Tile 2, Tile 3, Tile 4, Benefit. - 6.5–8 s: Short supported benefit sits beside the coherent system. Shows Brand color, Tile 1, Tile 2, Tile 3, Tile 4, Benefit detail. - 8–10 s: Final object and next step. Shows Brand color, Tile 1, Tile 2, Tile 3, Tile 4, Logo, Call to action. Use only facts the website or pages you read state. Never invent prices, discounts, dates, guarantees or claims. When a fact a field needs is missing, write a short placeholder in square brackets, such as [offer end date]. Make the three options clearly different in angle, wording and image choice. For images, choose real, large images of this brand and product: first from the page's own images (header logo, large files, feature-page screenshots), then with an image search. A social preview card (og:image, a title on a gradient) is a last resort. Give the direct URL of the image file, never a page URL, and never an image of another brand. Use an empty string when no image fits. If image search throws because no search backend is configured, tell the user in one sentence that a SerpAPI, DataForSEO or Brave key in Settings finds better images. Then take nodetool.web.screenshot of the product's feature pages instead. Save each image you consider as an asset and look at it with view_image before you offer it. Name in the option's description any image that is only a social preview card. Write `fillOptions` as a list of three objects, `fillChoice` as "" and `fillReport` as "". Each option: - value: "1", "2" or "3" - title: a name for the direction in 2 to 4 words - description: one sentence on what it emphasizes, then the first two copy lines in quotes - image: the URL of its first image, for the option card - brandColor: the brand's accent color as #RRGGBB (buttons, links, highlights), not the page background or a theme-color that is near black or white - fields: integrationProblem (Problem: hook, at most 7 words); connectionLabel (Connection line: assembly, at most 7 words); benefit (Benefit: resolve, at most 7 words); benefitDetail (Benefit detail: explain, at most 7 words); cta (Call to action: cta, at most 4 words) - images: tile1 (Tile 1: An icon or mark on a plain or transparent background. It shows small, as a node or tile, so it must read at about 200 px wide. Not a screenshot or a social preview card. Shown in: Separated tiles or a partly assembled object are already visible. | Tiles move toward their assigned cells. | The completed object rotates slightly or pulses once. | Short supported benefit sits beside the coherent system. | Final object and next step.); tile2 (Tile 2: An icon or mark on a plain or transparent background. It shows small, as a node or tile, so it must read at about 200 px wide. Not a screenshot or a social preview card. Shown in: Separated tiles or a partly assembled object are already visible. | Tiles move toward their assigned cells. | The completed object rotates slightly or pulses once. | Short supported benefit sits beside the coherent system. | Final object and next step.); tile3 (Tile 3: An icon or mark on a plain or transparent background. It shows small, as a node or tile, so it must read at about 200 px wide. Not a screenshot or a social preview card. Shown in: Separated tiles or a partly assembled object are already visible. | Tiles move toward their assigned cells. | The completed object rotates slightly or pulses once. | Short supported benefit sits beside the coherent system. | Final object and next step.); tile4 (Tile 4: An icon or mark on a plain or transparent background. It shows small, as a node or tile, so it must read at about 200 px wide. Not a screenshot or a social preview card. Shown in: Separated tiles or a partly assembled object are already visible. | Tiles move toward their assigned cells. | The completed object rotates slightly or pulses once. | Short supported benefit sits beside the coherent system. | Final object and next step.); logo (Logo: The brand's own logo file, such as the site header logo or its icon. Shown in: Final object and next step.) Then show the Start step with `only: ["fillChoice"]` and a one-sentence note, so the user sees just the option cards. Picking one runs `apply`, which saves the images and fills the steps.
